summary: Baileys fork pulls libsignal from unpinned GitHub source
details: This @izi-coder/baileys fork declares its libsignal dependency as `github:Cogils/libsignal-node` in package.json, with no version tag or commit SHA pinned. On `npm install`, npm fetches whatever the branch HEAD of that third-party GitHub repository currently serves and installs it into the dependency tree, where its own install lifecycle and any imports it exposes execute in the installer's environment. The source is a personal GitHub account rather than the official WhiskeySockets libsignal-node repository used by upstream Baileys, and there is no integrity constraint (no SHA pin, no npm registry resolution, no shasum check). A separate static match on `lib/Utils/generics.js` around a `ping` string in a generic connectivity-timing helper did not correspond to any exfiltration flow in this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
